## Who Counts as Unemployed?

The unemployment rate is calculated using the number of unemployed people divided by the combined number of employed and unemployed people—not everyone who lacks a job. Being jobless alone is not enough to be classified as unemployed.

A person must not have been employed during the survey’s reference week and must have been available for work, except in the case of temporary illness. In most cases, the person must also have actively searched for work during the four weeks ending with that reference week.

There is an exception for someone on temporary layoff who expects to be recalled. That person may qualify as unemployed without actively searching, provided the other conditions are met. By contrast, someone whose only job-search activity was browsing listings has not actively searched and does not qualify on that basis.

These conditions determine whether a person is counted among the unemployed—and included in the unemployment rate’s denominator.
